evidence.title: Hubba bint Hulail
evidence.text: Hubba bint Hulail was the grandmother of Hashim ibn' Abd Manaf, thus the great- great- great- grandmother of the Islamic" Nabī"( Prophet) Muhammad ibn Abdullah.

evidence.title: Ida of Lorraine
evidence.text: Ida of Lorraine( also referred to as Blessed Ida of Boulogne)( c. 1040 – 13 April 1113) was a saint and noblewoman.

evidence.title: Ida of Lorraine
evidence.text: She was the daughter of Godfrey III, Duke of Lower Lorraine and his wife Doda.

evidence.title: Ida of Lorraine
evidence.text: Ida's grandfather was Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine and Ida's brother was Godfrey IV, Duke of Lower Lorraine.

evidence.title: Nicolas, Duke of Mercœur
evidence.text: Nicolas of Lorraine, Duke of Mercœur (16 October 1524 – 23 January 1577) was the second son of Antoine, Duke of Lorraine and Renée de Bourbon.

evidence.title: Claude Françoise de Lorraine
evidence.text: Claude of Lorraine (6 October 1612 – 2 August 1648) was a daughter of Henry II, Duke of Lorraine, and Margerita Gonzaga, her sister was Nicole, Duchess of Lorraine.

evidence.title: Claude Françoise de Lorraine
evidence.text: She married her first cousin and was the Duchess of Lorraine by marriage.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: Gothelo( or Gozelo)( – 19 April 1044), called the Great, was the duke of Lower Lorraine from 1023 and of Upper Lorraine from 1033.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: He was also the margrave of Antwerp from 1005( or 1008) and count of Verdun.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: Gothelo was the youngest son of Godfrey I, Count of Verdun, and Matilda Billung, daughter of Herman, Duke of Saxony.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: On his father's death, he received the march of Antwerp and became a vassal of his brother, Godfrey II, who became duke of Lower Lorraine in 1012.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: He succeeded his brother in 1023 with the support of the Emperor Henry II, but was opposed until Conrad II forced the rebels to submit in 1025.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: When the House of Bar, which ruled in Upper Lorraine, became extinct in 1033, with the death of his cousin Frederick III, Conrad made him duke of both duchies, so that he could assist in the defence of the territory against Odo II, count of Blois, Meaux, Chartres, and Troyes( the later Champagne).

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: In the battle at Bar on 15 November 1037, Gothelo dealt a decisive blow to Odo, who was trying to create an independent state between France and Germany.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: Odo died in the battle.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: Gothelo died on 19 April 1044 and was buried in the Abbey Church of Bilzen.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: His son Godfrey succeeded in Upper Lorraine, but the Emperor Henry III refused to give him the duchy of Lower Lorraine as well.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: When Godfrey showed disagreement with the imperial decision, Henry III threatened to pass the duchy to Godfrey's incompetent brother Gothelo.

evidence.title: Gothelo I, Duke of Lorraine
evidence.text: This caused a long rebellion in Lotharingia between the allies of Godfrey( the counts of Flanders and Leuven) and imperial forces( 1044 – 1056).

evidence.title: Tjuyu
evidence.text: Tjuyu( sometimes transliterated as Thuya or Thuyu) was an Egyptian noblewoman and the mother of queen Tiye, and the wife of Yuya.

evidence.title: Tjuyu
evidence.text: She is the grandmother of Akhenaten, and great grandmother of Tutankhamun.

evidence.title: Godfrey I, Count of Verdun
evidence.text: Godfrey I (died 1002), called the Prisoner or the Captive ("le Captif"), sometimes the Old ("le Vieux"), was the count of Bidgau and Methingau from 959 and the count of Verdun from 963 to his death.

evidence.title: Godfrey I, Count of Verdun
evidence.text: In 969, he obtained the Margraviate of Antwerp and Ename.

evidence.title: Godfrey I, Count of Verdun
evidence.text: Between 974 and 998, he was also the count of Hainault and Mons.

evidence.title: Godfrey I, Count of Verdun
evidence.text: He was the son of Gozlin, Count of Bidgau and Methingau, and Oda of Metz.

evidence.title: Godfrey I, Count of Verdun
evidence.text: He was the brother of Adalberon, Archbishop of Reims, who crowned Hugh Capet the king of France.

evidence.title: Godfrey I, Count of Verdun
evidence.text: He was the founder of the House of Ardennes-Verdun, a cadet branch of the House of Ardennes.

evidence.title: Godfrey I, Count of Verdun
evidence.text: He was always loyal to the Ottonians, whom he was related through his maternal grandmother.

evidence.title: Bertha, Duchess of Lorraine
evidence.text: Bertha of Lorraine( or Bertha of Swabia)( b.c. 1123/30 – d. 1194/ 5) was a member of the Hohenstaufen dynasty.

evidence.title: Bertha, Duchess of Lorraine
evidence.text: She was the daughter of Frederick II, Duke of Swabia and, through marriage to Matthias I duke of Lorraine, she was duchess of Lorraine( c.1138-1176).

evidence.title: Charles Henri, Prince of Commercy
evidence.text: Charles Henri of Lorraine( 17 April 1649 – 14 January 1723) was the legitimated son of Charles IV, Duke of Lorraine, and Béatrix de Cusance.

evidence.title: Charles Henri, Prince of Commercy
evidence.text: He was given the Principality of Commercy in 1708 by his cousin Leopold, Duke of Lorraine.

evidence.title: Charles Henri, Prince of Commercy
evidence.text: He was also the Count of Falkenstein.

evidence.title: Renata of Lorraine
evidence.text: Renata of Lorraine( 20 April 1544 – 22 May 1602) was by birth a member of the House of Lorraine and by marriage Duchess of Bavaria.

evidence.title: Renata of Lorraine
evidence.text: Born in Nancy, France, she was the second child and eldest daughter of Francis I, Duke of Lorraine and Christina of Denmark.

evidence.title: Renata of Lorraine
evidence.text: Her paternal grandparents were Antoine, Duke of Lorraine and Renée of Bourbon- Montpensier and her maternal grandparents were Christian II of Denmark and Isabella of Austria.
